identity.title: Pain abrupt in onset and maximal at onset (thunderclap-type chest/back pain)

technique.how: Ask an open question about how the pain began, then specifically: 'Did it reach its worst within seconds, or build up over minutes?' Document time-to-peak intensity and whether the patient can pinpoint the moment of onset (what they were doing). Also ask about tearing/ripping quality and migration.
technique.prerequisites: Patient able to give history; otherwise ask witnesses or EMS about onset.

interpretation.positive_finding: Abrupt-onset pain is present in ~84-96% of aortic dissections but is common in other conditions, so it raises suspicion for dissection only modestly (specificity not established in unselected cohorts); it is a high-risk feature in the ADD risk score.
interpretation.negative_finding: Absence of sudden onset lowers the likelihood of dissection (LR- 0.3 in the RCE pooled series; 0.07 in an ED case-control study), but the clinical examination is insufficiently sensitive to rule out dissection on its own.
interpretation.pitfalls: Patients recall onset imprecisely, particularly after analgesia or when pain was preceded by exertion; gradual-onset presentations still occur in ~5-16% of dissections, especially in elderly patients or with painless neurologic presentations.
interpretation.changes_what: Positive: escalate to ADD-RS assessment, CXR/D-dimer and CT angiography as appropriate; negative onset lowers but does not eliminate dissection probability.

estimates.target_condition: Acute thoracic aortic dissection (finding: sudden-onset pain)
estimates.population: Consecutive patients with confirmed thoracic aortic dissection from 21 studies (case series; sensitivity pooled; LR- derived from comparison cohorts)
estimates.reference_standard: Dissection confirmed by imaging, surgery, or autopsy
estimates.quote: sudden onset (sensitivity, 84%). The absence of sudden pain onset lowers the likelihood of dissection (negative likelihood ratio [LR], 0.3; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.2-0.5)

estimates.population: Matched case-control: 194 ED/in-hospital CT- or echo-confirmed AAD cases vs 776 ED controls with truncal pain <14 days and no clear diagnosis
estimates.reference_standard: CT angiography or echocardiography confirmed dissection
estimates.quote: Absence of abrupt-onset pain (sensitivity = 95.9%, negative likelihood ratio = 0.07 [0.03-0.14]) can help rule out AAD.

sources.citation: Klompas M. Does this patient have an acute thoracic aortic dissection? JAMA. 2002;287(17):2262-2272.
Ohle R, Um J, Anjum O, et al. High risk clinical features for acute aortic dissection: a case-control study. Acad Emerg Med. 2018;25(4):378-384.
Ohle R, Kareemi HK, Wells G, Perry JJ. Clinical examination for acute aortic dissection: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Acad Emerg Med. 2018;25(4):397-412.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not use gradual onset alone to exclude dissection in patients with other high-risk features (Marfan/aortic disease, pulse deficit, neurologic deficit, new murmur, hypotension).
safety_scope.escalation_warning: Abrupt severe chest/back pain with hypotension, pulse deficit, or neurologic deficit is a dissection or ruptured AAA until proven otherwise: immediate CT angiography and surgical notification.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: Onset characterization depends on patient recall; the RCE pooled sensitivities from retrospective case series, and the case-control design (selected low-risk controls) likely inflates the LR- of 0.07.

extraction_notes: Klompas 2002 abstract gives pooled sensitivity 84% and LR- 0.3 (0.2-0.5) for sudden-onset pain; the LR+ and specificity are in the article tables, which were not accessible (JAMA, not open access), so they are null. Ohle 2018 case-control gives sensitivity 95.9% and LR- 0.07 but specificity was not in the abstract; case-control spectrum bias is flagged. The Ohle 2018 systematic review abstract does not report onset-related pooled values and is cited for context only. Verifier: check Klompas Table 2 for LR+ of sudden onset and Ohle 2018 case-control Table 2 for specificity.
